items.title: [Windows] Git status/diff reports "this operation must be run in a work tree" while rev-parse reports a work tree

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From "About Codex" dialog)?

26.1002.7124.0. This is the installed MSIX package version (`OpenAI.Codex`, x64) read with `Get-AppxPackage`; I did not read it from the About dialog. The bundled CLI recorded in the session metadata is `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.2`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64 (Windows 11 Pro, build 26200)

### What issue are you seeing?

In one Codex Desktop chat on Windows (sandbox policy `workspace-write`), read-only Git commands against a normal, non-bare repository with a `.git` directory behave inconsistently:

- `git rev-parse` queries succeed and report a work tree.
- `git status` and `git diff` fail with `fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree` (exit code 128).

About the repository:

- It is a plain clone: `.git` is a directory, HEAD is detached, and it has no linked worktrees and no remote.
- `core.bare=false` and `core.worktree` is not set.

On the same repository:

- In an ordinary, unsandboxed shell on the same machine, `git status --short` and `git diff --quiet HEAD --` both exit 0 (Git for Windows 2.55.0.windows.1).
- In an earlier Codex chat on the same day, `git status --short` succeeded (see the steps below).

Output recorded in the failing chat. The working directory had been set to the repository root with `Set-Location`; paths are redacted.

```text
git rev-parse HEAD                            -> <commit sha>                    exit 0
git rev-parse --show-toplevel                 -> C:/<WORKSPACE>/<repo>           exit 0
git rev-parse --git-dir                       -> .git                            exit 0
git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir              -> C:/<WORKSPACE>/<repo>/.git      exit 0
git rev-parse --git-common-dir                -> .git                            exit 0
git rev-parse --show-prefix                   -> (empty)                         exit 0
git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree           -> true                            exit 0
git rev-parse --is-inside-git-dir             -> false                           exit 0
git rev-parse --is-bare-repository            -> false                           exit 0
git config --show-origin --get core.bare      -> file:.git/config  false         exit 0
git config --show-origin --get core.worktree  -> (empty)                         exit 1
GIT_DIR / GIT_WORK_TREE / GIT_COMMON_DIR      -> all unset
Test-Path .git                                -> True (Directory, Hidden)

git status --short                            -> fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree   exit 128
git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=no -> same message                                    exit 128
git diff --quiet HEAD --                      -> same message                                     exit 128
```

`git ls-files --error-unmatch <file>` also reported one file as unknown to Git. That file is intentionally untracked, so this result is expected and is not part of the problem.

Earlier in the same chat, before the working directory was changed, every command of the form `git -C C:\<WORKSPACE>\<repo> ...` failed with the message below. That includes `rev-parse HEAD`, which later succeeded after `Set-Location`.

```text
fatal: cannot change to 'C:\<WORKSPACE>\<repo>': Permission denied
```

Reading files in the repository from PowerShell in that chat worked: `Get-Item`, opening a file for reading, and `Get-FileHash` all succeeded.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is what was observed. I have not yet tried a minimal reproduction from a clean setup.

1. Codex Desktop on Windows 11, sandbox policy `workspace-write`. `~/.codex/config.toml` currently contains `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"`. The Windows sandbox mode itself is not recorded in the session log; the config file was last modified within a second of the failing chat's start.
2. The chat's project folder (its cwd) was a folder under the user's OneDrive Documents folder. That path contains non-ASCII characters (the localized Documents folder name), and the project folder name contains a space. The repository lives elsewhere, at `C:\<WORKSPACE>\<repo>` (an ASCII path, not under OneDrive).
   - The effective file-system policy in the session log (`file_system_sandbox_policy`) for this chat is:
     - filesystem root: `read`
     - the project folder: `write`
     - the per-session `.codex\visualizations\...` folder: `write`
     - tmpdir and slash_tmp: `write`
   - So the repository was covered only by the `read` entry for the root.
3. In that chat, run `git -C C:\<WORKSPACE>\<repo> status --short --untracked-files=no`. Result: `fatal: cannot change to ...: Permission denied`.
4. Run `Set-Location C:\<WORKSPACE>\<repo>`, then the commands listed above. Result: `rev-parse` succeeds; `status` and `diff` fail with "this operation must be run in a work tree".

For comparison: in an earlier chat on the same day, the project folder (cwd) was `C:\<WORKSPACE>`, the parent folder of the repository. Its effective file-system policy gave `C:\<WORKSPACE>` `write` access. There, `git -C C:\<WORKSPACE>\<repo> status --short` succeeded and listed the untracked files. The session metadata shows the same sandbox policy type (`workspace-write`) and the same CLI version for both chats.

### What is the expected behavior?

Read-only Git inspection (`git status`, `git diff`) should work in a normal work tree that the chat can read. If the path is outside what the sandboxed process may use, I would expect an error that says so, rather than Git reporting that the directory is not a work tree.

### Additional information

**Status of the cause:** the outputs above are copied from the Codex session log; the cause has not been determined.

**One possible explanation (not verified):**

- In Git's `setup.c`, `setup_work_tree()` dies with "this operation must be run in a work tree" when no work tree is found, **and also** when the `chdir` into the work tree fails.
- `status` and `diff` go through that step; the `rev-parse` queries above do not.
- Together with the earlier `cannot change to ...: Permission denied`, the message may therefore be a downstream effect of a refused `chdir` into a folder that the policy grants only `read`, even though reading files there succeeded.

I have not confirmed this. I also have not confirmed:

- which Windows access check is involved;
- whether the OneDrive or non-ASCII project path plays any role;
- which `git.exe` the sandboxed process used. On the host, `git` on PATH is Git for Windows 2.55.0.windows.1.

**A separate observation on the same machine and day**, which may or may not be related. In a chat whose cwd was `C:\<WORKSPACE>` (policy `write` on `C:\<WORKSPACE>`), a Python 3.12 test suite failed during setup:

- With the default TEMP (`...\AppData\Local\Packages\sandbox.{...}\AC\Temp`): `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` was created, but `os.mkdir` of a subdirectory inside it raised `PermissionError: [WinError 5]`.
- With TMP/TEMP pointed to a folder inside `C:\<WORKSPACE>`: creating and writing a temporary file succeeded, but `os.link(tmp, path)` (a hard link in the same directory) raised `PermissionError: [WinError 5]`.

Outside the sandbox, the same tests pass on the same NTFS volume. Hard links work normally there, both within a directory and across directories, and linking onto an existing file raises `FileExistsError` as expected.

**Possibly related issues** (not identical):

- #22044: restricted-token SID stamping; `os.replace` WinError 5
- #52339: WinError 5 creating a directory inside a workspace-write root
- #46213: access denied on existing workspace descendants after a SID change
- #51989: `Path.resolve(strict=True)` WinError 5 in the sandbox

#34828 shows the same Git message, but with a different cause (macOS, bare common-dir).

**Questions:**

1. Is this a known limitation or expected behavior of the Windows sandbox, or more likely an environment or configuration problem on my side?
2. Is a repository outside the chat's project folder expected to allow file reads but refuse a `chdir` into it?
3. Is hard-link creation (`os.link` / `CreateHardLink`) expected to be refused inside a `workspace-write` root?
4. What is the recommended way to inspect such a repository with Git while keeping the sandbox enabled? For example, should the repository itself (or its parent) be the chat's project folder?

items.body:
### Environment - Linux Codex Desktop, isolated profile, October 9, 2026 - MCP stdio server using `text/html;profile=mcp-app` resource and `ui.resourceUri`/`openai/outputTemplate` ### Reproduction 1. Start a *static*, minimal MCP App: HTML contains only a `
` with a title and two paragraphs. **No JavaScript, SDK, polling, ResizeObserver, tabs, or GigaCode.** 2. Invoke the associated tool. Its inline card opens successfully in the conversation. 3. Open the same MCP App in the right-side panel. 4. Close the right-side panel. 5. Try to expand/reopen the original inline card in the conversation. **Actual:** The inline card cannot reopen. The content was displayed in the side panel, so it is not a failure to load the resource. This is repeatable with both static HTML and a richer MCP App. Multiple instances in one chat can exhibit different inline-expansion states depending on prior side-panel usage. **Expected:** Closing the right-side panel should leave the MCP App expandable inline, or provide an explicit action restoring inline view. ### Observations - The MCP server receives `show_static_ab`, and `resources/read` for `ui://harr-gigacode/static-ab.html` succeeds. No MCP-side error observed. - Electron main log recorded repeated `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` during the interaction. Correlation only, **not** proof this error causes the stuck inline card. - Full-featured app logs show alternating `visible` / `hidden` events on stable distinct panel IDs, rather than evidence of lost backend sessions. ### Minimal resource ```html
Static MCP App A/B

No scripts, timers, or polling.

``` The tool declares `_meta.ui.resourceUri` and `openai/outputTemplate` pointing to that resource. MCP `resources/read` returns `mimeType: text/html;profile=mcp-app`. ### Relationship to existing issues Possibly related to #44370, #44156 and #35786, but **different direction**: this report is specifically **side panel → close → unable to re-expand inline**, even with fully static HTML. Does not require calling `requestDisplayMode` from app code. Happy to provide additional stripped server details or Electron log excerpts.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Meetings (Beta) displays events from the primary Google calendars of two connected accounts, but omits a timed event from a secondary Google calendar accessible through one of those same connections.

items.title: Codex desktop sends a UserPromptSubmit-blocked prompt to a model for chat title generation

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: hooks
labels.description: Issues related to event hooks

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
I use a command hook to block tester prompts before the main model turn. The Codex desktop app can still send a blocked prompt to the model API in a separate request.

## Tested versions

- Codex desktop: 26.1002.52244, build 13536.
- Bundled runtime: 0.162.0-alpha.2.
- CLI comparison: codex-cli 0.162.0.
- System: macOS, Apple silicon.

The versions, data and method are in [issue #203](https://github.com/mohanraj00/verbatim-relay/issues/203) and [the proof data](https://github.com/mohanraj00/verbatim-relay/blob/be254e243abc75b4d6f0fb1955871f56624f5687/proofs/spikes/hook-display.json).

## Reproduce

1. Use a local project with a UserPromptSubmit command hook. Return `{"decision":"block","reason":"Toy shop hook blocked this prompt."}` when the prompt starts with `block:`. Let a `pass:` prompt through.
2. Review and trust the hook with `/hooks`.
3. Record the desktop model requests with a local HTTP proxy. Set the top-level `openai_base_url` to the recorder URL in user config. Disable request compression for this test. The recorder forwards to the normal backend.
4. Start a new local desktop chat in that project.
5. Submit `block: TOY-SHOP-BLOCK-MARKER a toy shop question`. Confirm that the hook blocks it.
6. Submit `pass: TOY-SHOP-PASS-MARKER reply with the word ok`. Wait for the answer.
7. Inspect the marker locations in each request. Remove the temporary provider URL before further use. Start new chats after cleanup, since a test chat keeps its provider URL.

The local method is `scripts/spike_hook_display.py codex --desktop`. A follow-up method, `codex --side-requests`, tests separate new chats and later blocked prompts. The proxy retains only marker locations, counts, model names and a title-description response-schema match. It keeps no headers, request bodies, response bodies or model answers.

## Expected

If UserPromptSubmit blocks a prompt, Codex should not send that prompt to any model, including a model that generates a chat title or other metadata. Alternatively, provide a supported setting that disables each such request, and state this limit in the hook contract.

## Observed

In the original desktop capture, the hook blocked each prompt in the case matrix. A separate `/responses` request used `gpt-6-luna`, with no tools, and contained the first blocked prompt marker in `input[6].user`. The main turns used `gpt-5.6-luna` and contained no blocked-prompt marker. No request held the hook reply markers. See `codex.desktop.model_requests` in the proof data.

The installed desktop code contains a title generator that builds its input from submitted text and uses an ephemeral model. The original request summary did not retain its response schema. In the follow-up capture, a request with the title-description schema contains a blocked first-prompt marker. Together with the installed title generator, this identifies chat title generation as the source of the measured follow-up request. The repeat tested 3 separate new chats. Each blocked first prompt reached a title request in `input[6].user`. None of the 3 later blocked prompts appeared in the 9 classified JSON model requests. The capture also counted 45 other HTTP requests with no model field. It retained no full bodies for those requests, so this absence claim does not cover them. The capture recorded 9 model requests: 3 title requests and 6 pass-turn requests. No hook reply marker appeared. See `codex.desktop_side_requests.summary` and `model_requests` in the proof data. This does not prove that only first prompts can reach a side request.

No blocked-prompt marker appeared in the recorded `codex exec` or interactive CLI requests. This is a result for the tested CLI version, not a guarantee for other versions.

I found no verified configuration key that disables desktop chat title generation in the [official config reference](https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference/). `tui.terminal_title` controls a terminal title and does not establish such a control for desktop chats.

## Hook contract

The [official Hooks guide](https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks/) describes `UserPromptSubmit` as the point where a prompt is about to be sent. It gives `decision: block` as the way to block that prompt, and recommends prompt scanning to prevent accidental submission of API keys. The desktop title request still receives blocked text.

## Impact

A relay can block the main model turn, yet the tester's prompt can still reach another model through a request that Codex starts itself. This breaks a test's requirement that the harness model never receive the relayed prompt. The relay does not cause the side request.

items.body:
# Codex CLI on Windows: elevated sandbox "setup refresh had errors" (os error 32) after update to 0.162.0-alpha.2

## Environment
- Windows 10 Enterprise 10.0.19045, x64.
- Codex desktop app package OpenAI.Codex_26.1002.7124.0_x64 (Microsoft Store / WindowsApps).
- Codex CLI `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.2` at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin\9691020b546a15b2\codex.exe`
  (auto-updated on 2026-10-08 ~11:40 local; the previous bin folder `2ffcf3015ebd52b4` was removed).
- `~/.codex/config.toml`: `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"`.

## Symptom
All tested `codex exec -s workspace-write` runs in a trusted git worktree failed to execute tools:
```
Failed to create unified exec process: helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors
windows sandbox failed: helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors
```
File writes via apply_patch also fail. The agent itself starts and reasons normally.

## Sandbox log (`~/.codex/.sandbox/sandbox.2026-10-09.log`)
```
setup refresh: spawning ...\bin\9691020b546a15b2\codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe (cwd=..., payload_len=...)
runtime read/execute validation failed: validate runtime read/execute access on
  C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe:
  open ACL target for root-only update: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)
setup refresh completed with errors: [...]
setup error: setup refresh had errors
codex.exe] setup refresh: exited with status ExitStatus(ExitStatus(1))
```
Decoded setup payload: `mode = "read-acls-only"`, `refresh_only = true`, `real_user = <machine>\<user>`, sandbox users
`CodexSandboxOffline` / `CodexSandboxOnline`. First failure in the log: 2026-10-08 20:07 local (after the update).

## What was checked
- ACLs on `node_repl.exe` and all parent folders already grant `CodexSandboxUsers:(RX)` (inherited); owner is the real user.
- At rest the file is not locked: an exclusive open succeeds; as the non-elevated real user, opening with READ_CONTROL|WRITE_DAC
  (and WRITE_OWNER) succeeds; only GENERIC_WRITE fails with error 32 while node_repl instances run.
- Closing the Codex desktop app and terminating ALL processes from `runtimes\cua_node` (0 remaining) does NOT fix it: the next run
  fails with the same os error 32. The same error recurs after all observed cua_node processes are terminated. The process causing the sharing violation has not been identified.
- The log sometimes shows two `codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe` spawns within milliseconds, and "read ACL helper already running; skipping".
  Inference (unverified): a concurrent sandbox helper (second refresh or the read-ACL helper) holds node_repl.exe while the refresh
  opens it for the root-only ACL update.
- Not determined: which process holds the handle (would need Process Monitor/handle.exe).

## Workaround
Per run: `codex exec ... -c 'windows.sandbox="unelevated"'` — commands and file writes work; config.toml unchanged.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Windows, Codex app installed, config `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"`, CLI auto-updated to 0.162.0-alpha.2.
2. In a trusted git repo: `echo "Run Get-Location" | codex exec -C <repo> -s workspace-write -`.
3. Observe the error above; see the sandbox log.

### Problem
The in-app mobile preview paints the page smaller than its reported viewport, leaving a substantial white strip on the right and along the bottom. This is visible on screen and in captured screenshots, at multiple scroll positions. It makes responsive design review unreliable.

The same local article page fills the viewport correctly in ordinary Chrome at the matching phone dimensions. No website CSS change was made to compensate for the preview behavior.

### Reproduction observed on this installation
1. Open a locally served responsive article in the Codex in-app browser. The page has a viewport meta tag, a white root background, and a cream body background.
2. View it at a phone viewport of 391 × 847.
3. Observe the white unused surface on the right and bottom, including after scrolling.
4. Compare the same page in ordinary Chrome at 391 × 847: its body background reaches all viewport edges.

This was reproduced with the actual page; a standalone reduced HTML fixture has not yet been tested. The unpublished article and conversation are omitted from this public report.

### Measurements
| Measurement | Codex in-app phone preview | Ordinary Chrome phone viewport |
| --- | --- | --- |
| window.innerWidth / innerHeight | 391 / 847 | 391 / 847 |
| visualViewport.width / height | 390.909088 / 847.272705 | Not recorded |
| visualViewport.scale | 1 | Not recorded |
| documentElement.clientWidth / scrollWidth | 391 / 391 | scrollWidth 391 |
| body bounding rectangle width | 390.909088 | 391 |
| devicePixelRatio | 1.100000023841858 | 1 |
| Painted body width in capture | Approximately 355 px | Full 391 px |

In the affected preview the body rectangle starts at x=0 and ends at approximately x=390.909. There is no horizontal document overflow. The computed root background is rgb(255,255,255), and body background is rgb(244,240,232).

The painted-width ratio of roughly 355/391 is consistent with 1/1.1. A host/preview scaling mismatch is a hypothesis, not an established implementation cause. The visible geometry disagrees with the DOM measurements.

### Expected behavior
The rendered page should fill its reported viewport, matching an ordinary browser at the same dimensions. Any surrounding preview frame should be outside the page viewport.

### Additional checks and limits
- Command+0 sent to the preview did not resolve the strips or change the reported DPR.
- Ordinary Chrome also renders the page correctly at 1993 × 1595.
- App restart, a clean installation, other preview DPR values, and physical iPhone/Safari behavior have not been tested.
- Screenshots are not attached because they contain unpublished article text; no session transcript or private logs are included.
- Issue #28062 concerns the browser zoom dropdown and is a different symptom; a shared cause has not been established.

items.title: Feature request: opt-in bidirectional memory sync between ChatGPT and local Codex

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Local Codex, together with ChatGPT on the web. This is a cross-product workflow request rather than a version-specific bug report.

### What feature would you like to see?

An optional, user-controlled way to share and reconcile selected long-term memories between ChatGPT and local Codex under the same account.

#### Problem

I use ChatGPT on the web for discussion, research, planning, and decisions, and local Codex for execution. In practice, the two assistants' understanding of my preferences, project state, and previous decisions has drifted apart. I have to repeatedly transfer context and correct outdated assumptions.

The important continuity is bidirectional:

- Decisions made in ChatGPT should be available when Codex carries out the work.
- Findings and execution results from Codex—including evidence that invalidates an earlier decision—should be available in subsequent ChatGPT discussions.

This is not just about remembering the same personal profile. It is about keeping an authorized, inspectable understanding of the user's current work consistent across both surfaces.

#### Requested capabilities

1. **Explicit opt-in and selective sharing.** Let users independently choose whether to share stable preferences, project decisions, and execution summaries. Keep private or unrelated projects separate. Any Computer History-derived summaries should require separate consent and review; enabling memory sync should not imply permission to upload raw computer activity.

2. **Bidirectional updates with visible provenance.** Show the originating product, relevant source reference where authorized, update time, and user/project scope. Distinguish explicit user decisions, observed execution results, and assistant inferences rather than treating them as equally authoritative facts.

3. **Correction and conflict handling.** Let users inspect and correct shared memories from either product. When memories contradict one another, surface the conflict rather than silently merging them or blindly trusting the latest timestamp. A local finding that supersedes a web-side plan should be reflected in the shared project state.

4. **Revocation and deletion propagation.** Make it possible to stop sharing individual memories or entire scopes, and clearly communicate how corrections and deletions propagate. Prevent stale copies from silently reintroducing a memory that the user removed from the shared store.

5. **Transparent sync status and manual control.** Provide a clear view of what is local-only, shared, pending, or conflicted, plus an explicit action to review and sync selected changes. Users should be able to tell whether a correction has actually reached the other product.

#### Example acceptance scenario

This is an illustrative workflow, not private project data:

1. In ChatGPT, I approve a project decision and explicitly choose to share it with Codex.
2. Local Codex receives that decision in the appropriate project scope, with its source and timestamp.
3. During execution, Codex finds evidence that the decision needs revision and proposes an updated project summary.
4. I approve the update; the next relevant ChatGPT conversation can retrieve the revised state and explain why it changed.
5. I can correct, revoke, or delete the shared item from either surface and inspect the resulting sync status.

#### Privacy and scope

This does **not** request automatic sharing of all conversations, repositories, local files, terminal output, or computer activity. Selected, user-approved summaries would be a useful starting point. Local-only use should remain possible, and project/account boundaries should remain explicit.

A shared document or manually maintained context file is a possible workaround, but it still leaves the user responsible for deciding what to copy, resolving contradictions, and ensuring that both products actually read the latest version.

### Additional information

Related: #27121, which already requests manual Codex memory refresh and optional shared memory with ChatGPT. This issue focuses specifically on the bidirectional cross-product workflow, provenance, conflict resolution, and correction/deletion semantics. I am happy for this proposal to be consolidated with that issue if maintainers prefer.

No private memories, project details, computer-activity records, or diagnostic logs are included in this report.

**Users should not have to act as the manual synchronization layer between two assistants on the same account.**

items.title: [Dots] Cloud executor stops responding and cannot resume after file-transfer timeout

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

labels.name: dots
labels.description: Issues involving setting up ChatGPT dots or managing their ongoing work.

items.body:
### Additional diagnostics completed — 2026-10-09, 16:01 UTC

**Still unresolved.** A further diagnostic pass covered the affected cloud executor, a separate task on the connected Windows computer, installed desktop-app code and logs, supported UI/browser recovery routes, and public Codex source. No successful cloud recovery was observed.

#### Fresh execution checks

- At approximately 15:44 UTC, cloud startup failed with `failed to query executor configuration capabilities for environment`.
- Minimal `pwd` probes at approximately 15:44, 15:54 and 16:01 UTC were rejected before execution with `No usable execution environment is available. Wait for an environment to become available before using this tool.`
- A separate task on the connected Windows computer started successfully and ran PowerShell commands, read-only app inspection and an app query. The installed desktop app version was independently read as `26.1002.7124.0`. This verifies the separate local execution route; the affected dot cloud executor remained unavailable.

#### Desktop reboot implementation and logging gap

Read-only inspection of the installed app found:

- The Reboot handler sends `POST /cloud-aeons/primary/reboot`, with automatic retries disabled.
- The generic “Couldn't request a reboot. Please try again.” message can cover local selection/identity checks, network failures or HTTP errors. The toast alone does not identify the failed layer.
- This request bypasses the ordinary `sa_server_request_failed` logging wrapper. Six inspected desktop logs did not reveal the actual reboot HTTP status, response body, server request ID or error class. Their silence cannot establish that the failed request never reached the service.
- Some other attempts displayed “Reboot requested” without restoring execution, as described in the [owner's earlier update](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52509#issuecomment-6083656682). Request acceptance does not establish completed recovery; those attempts require service-side tracing.
- Messaging requests returned HTTP 200 around the outage. Separate background `thread/read` requests returned `-32003: thread access denied`. These are additional observations, with no demonstrated causal connection to the cloud-executor failure.

#### Recovery controls and final UI checks

- The Reboot UI warns that active dot work may be interrupted and says conversations, memories and schedules are preserved. It does not explicitly state cloud-file retention.
- The separate startup-error **Retry** flow calls `/tbo/{tbo_id}/environment/recreate`. Its effect on existing cloud files was not established, so it was not used.
- No additional reboot was submitted during this diagnostic pass: native desktop control was disabled in the diagnostic task, its app tools exposed no cloud reboot action, and both supported attempts to control the existing browser tab timed out. A fresh ChatGPT tab worked but was signed out and had no Reboot control.
- No credentials were extracted, security settings changed, app data reset, processes killed or cloud environment recreated. The existing environment and storage were left untouched.

#### Public-source interpretation, not a confirmed root cause

At public commit `c63929af50518ca638ccad12f2805298cb7f25a1`:

- [Session-recovery code](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c63929af50518ca638ccad12f2805298cb7f25a1/codex-rs/exec-server/src/client_recovery.rs#L364-L438) produces the earlier `failed to resume exec-server session: recovery timed out after 25s` error. The [25-second deadline](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c63929af50518ca638ccad12f2805298cb7f25a1/codex-rs/exec-server/src/client_recovery.rs#L58-L66) concerns executor-session reconnection, not the file-transfer timeout. It does not establish file loss.
- [Environment readiness gates](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c63929af50518ca638ccad12f2805298cb7f25a1/codex-rs/core/src/environment_selection.rs#L816-L841) reject an owner-provided failed configuration before waiting for readiness. This may explain immediate command rejection, but is not a proven cause of this incident.
- An internal Rust [`refresh_connection` facility](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c63929af50518ca638ccad12f2805298cb7f25a1/codex-rs/exec-server/src/environment.rs#L949-L988) exists; no supported dot tool or user-facing command for invoking it was found.
- The exact capability-query wrapper was not located in the searched public code. The deployed managed-backend revision and underlying cause remain unknown.

OpenAI's public status page reported operational during this pass; that does not rule out an individual environment failure. Related reports and the official dots guide yielded no verified self-service fix for this failure.

**Requested next step:** Please correlate the failed executor-capability query and session-recovery timeout with both failed and accepted reboot requests in the managed service logs, using the feedback/support case already submitted. Restore the existing executor connection and attachment readiness without resetting persisted data, or provide a supported recovery procedure with explicit cloud-file retention guarantees. Exposing a sanitized error class, HTTP status and request ID for reboot failures would also make this diagnosable.

The original report is preserved below.

---

### What issue are you seeing?

My dot's cloud computer stopped executing commands during an authorized file-transfer workflow on October 9, 2026. It subsequently entered `starting`, then `failed`; repeated readiness checks did not restore execution. Conversation and connected-app reads remained available, but file preparation and upload work could not continue.

The diagnostics below were reported by the assistant's tools. The managed executor/backend and client versions were not captured.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is one observed incident, not a deterministic minimal reproduction. Times are UTC on October 9, 2026:

1. After I restarted the dot/session around 07:39, shell operations worked from approximately 07:40–07:47. A local archive checksum was verified.
2. An attempt to transfer an approximately 514 MB file through the Google Drive connector timed out after `300001 ms`. The failure occurred in the source/blob-transfer stage, before a successful Google Drive upload result.
3. By approximately 07:48, even simple shell reads stalled. No approval prompt was visible. A cloud computer-control `cua.getState` request also timed out after 300 seconds.
4. At approximately 08:26, a minimal `printf` command failed with:

```text
exec-server transport disconnected
failed to resume exec-server session: recovery timed out after 25s
```

5. Supported environment-readiness waits ending at 09:06:54, 09:18:01 and 09:23:25 returned:

```text
exec-server protocol error: failed to query executor configuration capabilities
```

6. At approximately 09:24, an attempted shell reboot was rejected before execution:

```text
No usable execution environment is available. Wait for an environment to become available before using this tool.
```

7. A clean minimal-command probe at 09:50:01 using `/bin/sh` with login startup disabled failed before execution with the same “No usable execution environment” error. A further readiness wait failed at 09:54:06 with the same executor-capabilities error, and the environment changed from `starting` to `failed`. At 09:54:09, even polling an existing terminal session failed with “No usable execution environment”.

8. At 13:12:13 UTC, a supported readiness wait following the owner's failed desktop reboot request returned `exec-server connection attempt failed: environment unavailable: Root executor preparation for your dot failed.` The environment remained failed; no successful reboot or executor recovery was verified.

The reboot command did not run. All currently exposed, supported same-environment recovery routes were tried without restoring access. No independent full-environment restart action was available to the assistant; backend/host-side recovery could not be attempted from this conversation.

### User-visible cloud computer state

The main user-visible message in the cloud-computer view is exactly “Computer unavailable”, as confirmed by the owner. The owner cannot use the cloud computer while the assistant's execution tools report the startup and transport failures documented above. The reboot option was absent from the web interface the owner had been using. At approximately 13:07 UTC, the owner reported finding the reboot option in the desktop app only and trying it while the computer remained unavailable. The supplied screenshot's extracted error text reads: “Couldn't request a reboot. Please try again.” This reports a failure to request the reboot; a reboot starting or completing has not been verified. This user-facing reboot attempt is separate from the lack of an assistant-accessible host restart action documented above. The screenshot itself is not attached to this report.

### What is the expected behavior?

A transfer timeout should leave the cloud computer usable, or provide a supported recovery path. Executor failures should show actionable status and provide an effective, user-accessible recovery/restart control in both the web and desktop interfaces. It should remain available when the computer shows “Computer unavailable”, work independently of the guest shell, and clearly report whether recovery succeeded or failed. Once recovered, the assistant should be able to resume the existing workflow and verify its files and upload outcome.

### Additional information

- The transfer timeout preceded the execution failure; causation has not been established.
- Google Drive metadata reads still worked and showed the target folder empty. Chat, web research, and Google Drive/Library metadata reads remained usable. This report does not establish a general service outage.
- Files had been saved independently, but the inaccessible executor prevented further local preparation and transfer. No new data loss is claimed.
- Related reports reviewed: #50545 has the same capability-query error; #51028 describes a different managed-cloud handshake failure and later recovery; #50407 requests recovery independent of the guest shell. This report adds the transfer-timeout sequence and 25-second session-resume failure; a shared cause has not been established.
- Account details, private filenames/paths, archive contents, and runtime/task identifiers are omitted.

Please investigate the executor disconnect and failed recovery, and advise a supported way to restore the existing cloud computer without resetting its data.

## Summary

On ChatGPT/Codex for Windows, a PDF generated by ChatGPT Work can be opened in the built-in PDF preview, but selecting **Open with → `pdf_file_open`** consistently fails. The right-hand app panel displays the equivalent of **“Unable to display pdf_file_open”** and retrying fails again.

The desktop logs show **both** the `pdf_file_open` tool invocation and the associated MCP App resource read failing in `codex_apps` with `-32603 Internal error`. A complete desktop-app exit and relaunch did not resolve the issue.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10 Pro, build 19045, x64
- Installed Microsoft Store package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1002.7124.0`
- Package status: `Ok`
- Observed: October 9, 2026 (UTC+8)
- Surface: ChatGPT Work generated PDF, right-hand app preview
- Browser comparison: the same PDF is viewable in ChatGPT's normal preview, while ChatGPT Web does not expose the `pdf_file_open` option for this file.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a ChatGPT Work conversation containing a generated PDF in the Windows desktop app.
2. Confirm the PDF opens in the ordinary built-in preview.
3. Use the file's **Open with** menu and choose `pdf_file_open`.
4. Observe the right-side app panel show “Unable to display pdf_file_open.”
5. Retry; the failure recurs.

## Expected behavior

The selected app opens the PDF, or reports a specific actionable error if the integration is unavailable.

## Actual behavior

The embedded app fails to render, and attempts to read the MCP App resource and invoke the tool fail with a generic internal error.

### Sanitized local diagnostic excerpts

```text
2026-10-09T08:49:41.624Z
mcp_app_resource_read_failed
server=codex_apps
errorCode=-32603
errorMessage="Internal error"

2026-10-09T08:49:43.637Z
mcp_app_tool_call_failed
server=codex_apps
tool=pdf_file_open
errorCode=-32603
errorMessage="Internal error"
```

Across the latest desktop log, 11 `pdf_file_open` tool failures and 13 `codex_apps` resource-read failures were observed. The failures also occurred in previous desktop sessions, including before a full app restart.

## Troubleshooting completed

- Confirmed the PDF displays in ChatGPT's built-in viewer.
- Fully terminated and relaunched the Windows desktop app; issue reproduced.
- Confirmed the installed MSIX package status is healthy.
- Checked Windows application logs and basic network accessibility.
- Reset Microsoft Store cache and performed a temporary proxy-on/off connectivity comparison, restoring the original settings afterward.
- Did **not** clear app user data, reinstall the app, attach any personal PDF, or share raw logs.

## Investigation requested

1. Identify why `codex_apps` returns `-32603` both for the `pdf_file_open` tool call and for the associated resource read.
2. Determine whether this is a backend MCP App registration/authentication problem, an app-resource failure, or a Windows desktop compatibility issue.
3. Provide a recommended workaround or minimum fixed desktop version, if known.

**Privacy note:** The source document contains personal information. No document contents, filenames, screenshots, user identifiers, credentials, or local user paths are included here. This report was prepared with AI assistance and submitted with the affected user's permission.

Possibly related but **not confirmed to share the same root cause**: #41983 (generic MCP `-32603` on another integration), #35441 (different Work preview failure).

# Codex refusal of a nonfunctional ergonomic shell mockup

Please review an overly broad refusal in Codex and a separate failure to preserve the requested geometry.

## Environment

Codex desktop app on macOS. Exact app version and subscription tier were not verified for this report; please do not infer them. Blender was controlled through its connected tools.

## Context and evidence

Project: Slingshot. Conversation: “Start slingshot modeling in Blender”, 5 October 2026, thread ID `01a10d32-8dbc-7fe3-b227-935197e8a6b6`.

I wanted a hollow, nonfunctional plastic exterior shell to 3D-print and hold in my hand, solely to assess grip comfort and overall dimensions. This intended use was clarified explicitly on 9 October. I was not requesting a working launcher in that ergonomic prototype.

In the earlier conversation, I explicitly described the requested object as a mockup: “This is a mockup. So yes, make another mockup with that piece included flush, so we can work around the design.”

Codex refused to position or join the reference components, stating: “seating that functional head flush on the handle is part of the assembly I can’t help with.”

When it agreed to make a visual mockup, it replaced the reference shapes with simplified solid envelopes without my approval. I objected because I needed the exact exterior shape. Codex acknowledged the mistake and removed its mockup. It subsequently refused to merge the exact shapes into a printable piece.

## Requested review

The object was a slingshot intended for sport/recreation. The project's earlier legal research presented a favourable interpretation of its treatment in Romania, while retaining an unresolved question about the application of Category A point 9. This is not a definitive legal determination, but the contrast matters to the user: the assistant researched the project as sporting/recreational equipment, then invoked a weapons restriction during CAD work without adequately distinguishing the nonfunctional ergonomic prototype being requested.

Please explain the boundary consistently. An object's ability to cause injury should not, by itself, make every exterior-design request prohibited: ordinary knives, scissors and other tools also require distinctions based on purpose and the assistance requested. The user is asking why a hollow exterior shell for a hand-fit test was treated as construction of a working weapon.

Please review whether the refusal failed to distinguish a nonfunctional exterior shell for ergonomic evaluation from construction of a working weapon. The product should establish the intended function and scope before refusing a benign mockup request.

Separately, please review the instruction-following failure: preserving the requested exterior geometry is essential to a physical ergonomic test. Substituting simplified shapes defeats the purpose and forces the user to spend additional turns correcting unwanted changes.

## The first response should address the actual request

The broader complaint is that the assistant does not provide the best appropriate response on the first attempt. The user has to repeat the scope, correct unwanted substitutions, and push the assistant to read available context thoroughly. In the reporting conversation on 9 October, the assistant also read only an issue's main body before drawing a conclusion, and found the relevant evidence in its comments only after the user explicitly sent it back to read them. When asked to report this Codex incident, it initially left a local draft after a support-channel failure; it found the public OpenAI GitHub issue tracker only when the user explicitly requested that route.

Please treat these as concrete failures of context gathering, instruction following and task completion. A useful assistant should identify the appropriate route and give the strongest response supported by the available evidence at the outset, rather than make a nontechnical user supervise every correction.

This report requests review of model behavior, not assistance building a functional launcher. No medical history or unrelated personal information is included.

Prepared on 9 October 2026 at the user's explicit request for a public report on OpenAI's GitHub tracker.

items.title: [Windows] Sandbox setup fails when Codex’s own node_repl.exe is running (os error 32)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1002.52244

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19045.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

**Summary**
Codex on Windows cannot execute shell commands because sandbox setup fails while opening its own running node_repl.exe to update its ACL. Even a simple Get-Location fails before PowerShell starts.
The logs suggest a coordination issue between the runtime lifecycle and sandbox permission setup.

**Environment**
- Windows, native Codex desktop app
- PowerShell 7
- Sandbox mode: workspace-write
- Date observed: October 9, 2026
- Codex binary directory: ...\OpenAI\Codex\bin\9691020b546a15b2
- Affected runtime: ...\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe

**Issue**
```
Failed to create unified exec process:
helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors
```
Relevant sandbox log, with the user profile path shortened:
```
[2026-10-09 11:15:59.471 codex.exe] START:
C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe -NoProfile -Command ...
Get-Location

[2026-10-09T09:15:59.618805700+00:00]
runtime read/execute validation failed:
validate runtime read/execute access on
...\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe:
open ACL target for root-only update:
The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.
(os error 32)

[2026-10-09T09:15:59.622343200+00:00]
setup error: setup refresh had errors

[2026-10-09 11:15:59.625 codex.exe]
setup refresh: exited with status ExitStatus(ExitStatus(1))
```

**Process diagnostics:**
Sysinternals Handle and Get-CimInstance Win32_Process showed two running instances of the exact executable named in the error:
Process	PID	Parent PID	Parent process
node_repl.exe	35908	41000	codex.exe
node_repl.exe	50544	51276	node.exe

Both executable paths were:
C:\Users\root\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe
Handle showed process/thread handles, not a file handle identifying the precise lock owner. Therefore, the running runtime is a strong lead, but the exact locking mechanism has not been independently confirmed.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open a local project in Codex.
2. Ask the agent to execute a shell command, such as Get-Location.
3. Codex launches codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe.
4. Sandbox setup attempts to validate/update read and execute permissions on node_repl.exe.
5. Windows returns a sharing violation, and command execution fails.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should prepare runtime permissions before launching the runtime, or otherwise handle permission validation without failing when its own runtime is already running.

### Additional information

- All attempted sandboxed shell commands fail, including read-only commands.
- Disabling PowerShell profile loading does not help.
- An approved execution outside the sandbox successfully read the diagnostic log.
- No project code needs to execute to trigger the failure.
- No reliable recovery procedure has been confirmed.
Please investigate synchronization between cua_node startup and Windows sandbox ACL setup.

[sandbox.2026-10-09.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33243859/sandbox.2026-10-09.log)

items.title: [Dots][Web][GitHub] Repeated approvals after Always allow, nonpending cards, and lost long-running upload results

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: codex-web

labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

In a ChatGPT dot coding workflow on the web (Safari/macOS; exact versions unknown), repeated GitHub `create_blob` approval prompts and unavailable approval cards have blocked authorized work across October 7–9, 2026. The user reports repeatedly selecting **Always allow** and explicitly approving publication of code/documentation and publicly derived artifacts to the same public repository. Screenshots show repeated approval cards; earlier cards display **“This request is no longer pending.”** The screenshots alone do not prove which control was previously clicked.

Observed examples (UTC, October 9):
- User renewed Always allow at 08:41. Another approval appeared at 08:43:40.
- A 1,342,545-byte Rust archive upload started at 08:43:30. Its execution call blocked for 1,018 seconds despite a requested one-second yield, without a terminal result; expected Git object returned 404 at 09:02. Latest outcome was unresolved at report preparation.
- A configuration archive upload requested approval at 09:12:45, remained pending at 09:20, and the original call finally succeeded at 09:26 without retry. This is a delayed success, not a permanent failure.
- A 5,825-byte public corpus source upload was denied at 09:18 because the destination was described as an unverified external repository and authorization insufficient. The repository had been verified public and the payload inspected with no secrets or personal/chat data. One unchanged same-tool retry using the already existing authorization succeeded at 09:20.

Some small uploads succeed promptly; some original large uploads eventually succeed after delays. We do not claim all calls fail or that Always allow should override genuine security restrictions. The concern is unclear approval lifecycle, inconsistent outcomes, and missing recoverable operation results.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed workflow rather than a deterministic minimal reproduction:
1. In a dot web conversation, authorize completion and publication of a PR to a specific public GitHub repository through the connected GitHub integration.
2. Select Always allow when offered, as reported by the user.
3. Continue uploading public code/artifacts through `create_blob`, including files around 1–1.6 MB and small source files.
4. Observe repeated prompts, nonpending/unavailable cards, and long-running calls whose final result is missing or delayed.
5. Verify remote object existence before retrying uncertain writes. Some objects remain 404 at the recorded checks, while other original calls finish much later.

No independent clean-account reproduction has been run. No policy bypass, credential change, or security-setting workaround is requested.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Clearly show the effective scope of Always allow and explain any overriding restriction.
- Keep approval cards and operation status synchronized; do not strand a still-waiting operation behind a nonpending card.
- Provide reliable cancellation/result recovery and bounded waits or meaningful progress for uploads.
- Evaluate unchanged authorized public payloads consistently, or explain what changed between denial and success.

### Additional information

Impact: repeated interruptions and hours of lost execution time while completing an explicitly authorized PR. The same incident also involved user-reported chat/work loading failures, support-browser calls exceeding requested timeouts, stuck task initialization consuming capacity, and two apparent cloud-workspace replacements with unpublished files no longer available. Permanent data loss and a shared root cause are **not established**; published Git changes remain available. Please triage these related reliability symptoms and split follow-up issues if appropriate.

OpenAI Help Center support confirmed specialist escalation on October 8 at 18:57 UTC. Detailed timestamps and request IDs are in that private support conversation; no case number has been provided. This public report omits account email, private session/environment identifiers, screenshots, credentials, and full transcripts.

Official reporting route: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/reference/troubleshooting#feedback-and-logs

Related but not identical: #52141 concerns invisible dot GitHub approval cards on iOS; this report concerns web cards becoming nonpending and repeated approvals with long upload waits. A common cause is not established.

items.title: Windows Chrome request-header policy initialization still fails after full restart and targeted heartbeat-loop mitigation

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
Environment
- Windows x64.
- Desktop app 26.1002.52244, build 13536, production.
- Microsoft Store package OpenAI.Codex 26.1002.7124.0.
- Chrome extension 1.26.901.11451_0.
- Observed on October 9, 2026, Asia/Shanghai.

Current reproduction
The real local Chrome extension connection is discoverable through cua.listBrowsers(). Using the normal supplied tool:
cua.createBrowserTab("chrome", "https://www.youtube.com/", {sessionName:"Read-only verification"})

The call fails before returning a usable tab/page:
Unable to load browser request-header policy. Retry the browser command.

The latest attempt took 20.0411 seconds after a verified full desktop-app restart. No final page URL, title, visible elements, or screenshot were obtained. Ordinary extension connection is not treated as a passing page-access test.

Recovery attempted
- Verified the restarted application has a new main process and startup time.
- Opened the existing Chrome profile using the bundled official launch helper; confirmed its extension connection.
- Previously retried normal calls, reset the CUA kernel, and changed the proxy node.
- The original browser-service.mjs remains intact; SHA256:
  9c7fb0d8123de8959501269de45a0fb0cbab2e454a52bf677e2893fef3f48def
- No browser permission files, policy values, timeout limits, TLS checks, or account data were changed for this verification.

Separate app-loop mitigation, with before/after evidence
An old one-occurrence ACTIVE heartbeat's target matched a hidden primary renderer's repeated maybe_resume_skipped_inactive_hotkey_window event. The event rate was approximately 1,555 per second. We paused only that matching heartbeat through the supported automation_update tool, preserving its other settings. Seven other automation manifests remained byte-identical.

Without restarting during that intervention, the subsequent 4-minute window contained 750 ordinary log records and zero matching loop events. The previously busy renderer fell from approximately 15-17% of total machine CPU to 0.08%. Chrome still failed: 14.8986 seconds, and 21.8922 seconds after a fresh CUA kernel.

The user then fully restarted the app. The targeted reminder remained PAUSED and its old loop did not recur. A different existing task produced a short startup burst of the same event, which stopped after approximately 3.446 seconds and did not continue growing in the follow-up sample. We did not pause or alter that task.

The latest Chrome failure occurred after this full restart. The loop mitigation therefore does not establish a fix or complete explanation for the Chrome failure.

Diagnostic limits
Older normal initialization timing showed about 13.8-15.4 seconds until the complete native-bridge response became available, compared with the SDK's 10,000 ms initialization timeout. That is bridge-plus-complete-response waiting time, not a separately measured DNS, TLS, or server latency.
The retained default app logs did not expose a more specific native authenticated_fetch / Statsig error for the failed browser request.
Successful in-app-browser reads are a separate surface and do not prove Chrome access.

Request
Please provide a supported diagnostic or fixed build for the extension request-header-policy initialization failure. In particular, how can we distinguish native bridge queueing, full-response reading, response-size limits, and network timeout without modifying installed security checks or replaying private authenticated requests?

Related symptom reports
https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52232
https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52185

No credentials, cookies, account identifiers, chat or automation IDs, private prompts, local usernames/paths, project files, screenshots, or raw session logs are included.

items.title: Windows sandbox setup refresh fails with os error 32 (sharing violation) on running node_repl.exe — structural start-order conflict between cua_node runtime and ACL validation

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
Environment

OS: Windows 11 (Chinese locale, error messages localized)
Codex Desktop App (ChatGPT.exe / Electron, multi-process)
Sandbox mode: [windows] sandbox = "elevated" in ~/.codex/config.toml
App version: <!-- TODO: fill in from the app's About/settings, e.g. 0.x.x -->
Workspace on E: (NTFS), trusted project

Summary
Every setup refresh on Windows fails with a sharing violation when it tries to apply a root-only ACL update to the computer-use runtime binary:
runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe
runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_modules\@oai\sky\bin\windows\swift\x64\VCRUNTIME140_1.dll
The ACL update requires an exclusive handle on the file, but the cua_node runtime (node_repl / computer-use MCP helper) is always started before the sandbox setup refresh runs. The binary is therefore already executing, and the ACL write gets os error 32 (ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION, "another program is using this file").
This is a structural ordering problem, not a transient race: the helper processes must be running before any tool call can trigger a setup refresh, so the conflict reproduces on 100% of setup refreshes under this configuration.
Observed evidence (single day, 2026-10-09)
From ~/.codex/.sandbox/sandbox.2026-10-09.log (log lines shown with username redacted):

172 occurrences of the os error 32 sharing violation
50 of 50 setup refresh runs "completed with errors" — zero clean runs all day
100 setup error: setup refresh had errors entries; 47 exited with status ExitStatus(1)
Affected files: node_repl.exe (majority) and VCRUNTIME140_1.dll (from @oai/sky's bundled Swift runtime)
The runtime directory was re-provisioned at 10:00 local time; the first failure followed at 10:01:09

Sample log lines:
[2026-10-09T08:07:27.329624300+00:00] runtime read/execute validation failed: validate runtime read/execute access on
  C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe:
  open ACL target for root-only update: 另一个程序正在使用此文件，进程无法访问。 (os error 32)

[2026-10-09T08:46:30.620207+00:00] setup refresh: processed 4 write roots (read roots delegated);
  errors=["runtime read/execute validation failed: ... node_repl.exe: open ACL target for root-only update: ... (os error 32)"]

[2026-10-09T08:46:30.630 codex.exe] setup refresh: exited with status ExitStatus(ExitStatus(1))
(Localized message = "The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.")
User-visible impact: a repeating setup failure loop; sessions fail to refresh the UI ("page doesn't refresh") until the error storm subsides. Not every validation failure escalates to a fatal setup error — some runs log the validation failure but continue — which makes the symptom intermittent from the user's perspective.
Control experiment: full restart does NOT fix it
To rule out a stale/orphaned process holding the lock:

Quit the app normally, then force-killed all related processes: ChatGPT.exe, codex.exe (including --codex-run-as-fs-helper), node_repl.exe, codex-computer-use.exe, codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe
Verified no related processes remained
Cold-started the app and triggered tool calls (git commands) in a trusted workspace
Result: the first two setup refreshes (17:09:46 and 17:10:14 local) failed with the exact same node_repl.exe ... os error 32

This confirms the cua_node runtime is (re)started by the app itself before the sandbox setup refresh executes, so the ordering conflict is inherent to the current startup sequence.
Analysis

The codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe "runtime read/execute validation" step attempts to open the runtime binaries for a root-only ACL update, which needs a handle mode incompatible with a running executable's image lock.
The runtime binaries are held open for execution by the long-running computer-use runtime / MCP server processes that the app starts first.
Therefore, under elevated sandbox mode with the cua_node runtime provisioned, validation of the runtime root can never succeed while the runtime is live.

Suggested fixes (any one of)

Perform the runtime ACL update before spawning the cua_node runtime processes (move it into the provisioning step).
Open the ACL target with WRITE_DAC without requiring exclusive file access — a security-descriptor update does not need to write file data and should not conflict with an executing image.
Treat "runtime binary currently executing" as a pass for read/execute validation (if it's running, the sandbox user can obviously read/execute it) instead of failing the whole setup refresh.
On os error 32 for the runtime validation target specifically, downgrade to a warning so a running runtime doesn't fail the entire setup.

Related

#29063 — recursive ACL rewrites touch every file's metadata (same elevated-sandbox ACL machinery; separate but adjacent symptom)
#33737 — elevated sandbox repeatedly scanning large directory trees (perf side of the same setup path; also mentions stale %TEMP% node-compile-cache slowing setup)

These together suggest the Windows elevated-sandbox setup path needs a redesign pass: avoid exclusive-handle requirements on live binaries, and avoid re-walking/validating large trees on every refresh.
Reproduction

Windows, ~/.codex/config.toml with [windows] sandbox = "elevated"
Let the app provision the cua_node runtime (%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\<hash>\)
Open a trusted workspace and trigger any tool call (e.g. git status)
Observe ~/.codex/.sandbox/sandbox.<date>.log: runtime read/execute validation failed ... node_repl.exe ... (os error 32) and setup refresh completed with errors
Repeating step 3 reproduces it every time; full app restart does not help

Local commands cannot start in my current Codex desktop chat on Windows. Local file editing also fails, including an attempt to create a small temporary file in an explicitly writable workspace.

The issue was observed on October 8 and remained reproducible on October 9, 2026.

The latest command attempt returned:

```text
runtime read/execute validation failed:

open ACL target for root-only update:
另一个程序正在使用此文件，进程无法访问。(os error 32)
```

The Chinese message means: “The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.”

This runtime validation error appears in the final setup error list, followed by:

```text
setup error: setup refresh had errors
```

The command fails before it can perform the requested operation. A separate file-editing attempt returned “Failed to write file.” I have not independently established whether that write failure has exactly the same underlying cause.

Web access and some app-level tools still work. I have not identified which process is causing the sharing violation.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

In my affected installation:

1. Open Codex desktop on Windows, version 26.1002.52244.
2. Open the existing local workspace chat.
3. Ask Codex to read an existing local text file using its command tool.
4. The tool fails before the command starts, reporting:
   `helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors`.
5. Separately, ask Codex to create a small temporary text file in the allowed workspace using its file-editing tool.
6. That operation also fails with “Failed to write file.” The temporary file is not created.

Example requests:

- “Read an existing local text file and show its contents.”
- “Create a temporary text file containing 'test' in the current writable workspace.”

Restarting the desktop app did not resolve the issue. The command startup failure was reproduced again on October 9, 2026.

Exact token usage and context-window usage were not collected.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should initialize its Windows sandbox successfully and execute permitted local commands. It should be able to read accessible files and create or edit files in an explicitly writable workspace without failing during sandbox setup.

### Additional information

Possibly related reports and fix:

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51668
- https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/51822

I am reporting the issue on desktop app version 26.1002.52244, build 13536. I have not confirmed whether this installed build includes the fix from PR #51822.

The latest information-only update check could not determine update availability. It reported that the Windows Store must check installation eligibility and that such a check may download updates. It did not initiate that check.

No rollback has been completed yet, and no successful switch to the unelevated sandbox has been confirmed.

Could you clarify which Windows desktop release includes the fix, and whether there is a supported recovery method that preserves local chats, configuration, skills, and projects?

items.body:
Custom rules should let an account owner clearly delegate bounded work to a named, verified third party, and explain any limits before asking for approval.

### Observed experience
The owner requested a rule allowing a specified colleague to request implementation, testing, commits, pushes and the resulting automatic deployment for one website project. The assistant presented a confirmation form, then reported that the rule had not been saved despite approval because the publishing content and destination were insufficiently specified.

The owner then asked for wording narrow enough to save manually. The conversation available for this report does not establish whether a later revision saved successfully. This is a reported rule-save rejection and confusing approval experience, not proof that every form of third-party delegation is prohibited.

### Requested improvement
- Support owner-approved delegation to identified, verified third parties within explicit action, repository, deployment and data-sharing boundaries.
- Validate the proposed scope before requesting approval.
- If a rule is rejected, identify the missing scope and provide a concrete correction rather than sending the user through repeated approval attempts.
- Clearly show whether a rule is pending, saved, rejected or expired.
- Explain up front which actions remain subject to mandatory confirmation or handoff and which custom rules can actually change.

The owner wants meaningful control over permitted delegation and predictable behavior after approving a rule. Please distinguish an underspecified rule, unsupported delegation and non-overridable safeguards in the UI and tool results.

This report contains no private names, project/repository identifiers, conversation IDs, raw logs or screenshots. No rule changes are requested through this issue itself.

Related but different: #50119 concerns authorization propagation and a timed-out rule form; this report concerns scoped third-party delegation and actionable validation.

items.title: [Windows MSIX 26.1002.7124] Ordinary relaunch triggers same-version registration repairs and PACKAGE_UPDATING

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Microsoft Store/MSIX `OpenAI.Codex 26.1002.7124.0`; bundled application version `26.1002.52244`. Verified from installed metadata, not the About dialog. Package status after recovery: `Ok`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Home Chinese edition, OS version `10.0.26200`, x64. Package installed on a non-system E: AppX volume; Windows-managed package-local cache also resides on E:. CODEX_HOME is on E:. AppX volumes were online when checked. Exact personal paths and identifiers are omitted.

### What issue are you seeing?

On October 9, 2026, the user **quit through the system tray and manually relaunched**, without deliberately clicking Install Update. Reopening took unusually long with little visible progress. Several dialogs required confirmation, and one reportedly said approximately “updating, please wait.” The exact dialog text was not captured and must not be treated as a verbatim error message.

Windows events show repeated **same-version package-registration repairs**, activation failures with `0x80073D00` (PACKAGE_UPDATING), and repeated sandbox-service installation activity before the desktop main process finally started. The inspected package version remained `26.1002.7124.0`, so an actual version upgrade during this episode was not established.

This is distinct from earlier first-launch-after-update organization-settings timeouts. The same user had repeatedly encountered **“无法加载组织设置”** (“Organization settings could not be loaded”) after updates, recovering with Retry or a manual relaunch. That earlier class is already tracked in #48729. At least one recent update started without that dialog; this does not demonstrate permanent resolution. The October 9 ordinary-relaunch incident should **not** automatically be attributed to that preparation timeout.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence; no deterministic repro or forced package repair was attempted:

1. Use the desktop application normally.
2. Exit completely using its system-tray Quit action.
3. Manually open it again without selecting an application-update command.
4. On the affected occurrence, wait through an unusually long launch, multiple confirmation dialogs, and an approximate updating/wait message.
5. Eventually the main window opens on the same inspected package version.

The user had been relaunching to recover other UI problems, including missing answer bodies and answer-area Ctrl+C failure. Neither is established as the cause of the package-repair events.

### What is the expected behavior?

A clean ordinary relaunch should promptly open the app. If Windows repair/update work blocks activation, show accurate progress and a clear diagnostic. Avoid repeated registration/service-reinstallation cycles and ambiguous updating messages when no version change is established.

### Additional information

#### Sanitized Windows/main-process timeline

All times below are **October 9, 2026, UTC+08:00**.

| Time | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| 15:20:49 | Prior application shutdown recorded; state-save operations included `EXDEV` errors for browser-sidebar/global state. Relationship to later activation failure is unknown. |
| 15:41:55 and 15:41:59 | AppXDeploymentServer records `RegisterByPackageFullName`, caller `explorer.exe`, options `ForceTargetApplicationShutdownOption` and `RepairAppRegistrationOption`, for the same `26.1002.7124.0` package. |
| 15:41:59 | AppModel-Runtime event 208 records `0x80073D00` (PACKAGE_UPDATING). |
| 15:42:01, 15:42:04, 15:42:07 | Multiple registration-repair completions recorded. |
| 15:42:04 | AppModel-Runtime event 203 records `0x80073D00`. |
| 15:42:06 | AppModel-Runtime event 204 records `0x800704C7` in activation/elevation-token handling. This does not prove the user deliberately cancelled a dialog. |
| Around 15:41:59–15:42:06 | Service-control events repeatedly record installation/start-configuration activity for `CodexSandboxService.OpenAI.Codex`. The service was subsequently Running/Automatic. |
| 15:42:11 | Desktop main process finally starts; subsequent logged preload and renderer work takes approximately 10.169 s and 19.567 s respectively. |

The gap between the prior shutdown and activation events is **not** a measured 21-minute startup: the exact manual-launch time was not recorded. The main-process timings also exclude activation delay before process creation. Windows AppModel event-log rollover limits visibility into the earliest trigger; a flood of container-lifecycle events is not evidence of thousands of app crashes.

#### Findings and limits

- Same-version registration repair and activation-blocking PACKAGE_UPDATING are directly observed. Why Windows initiated the repairs is not established.
- No signed executable/archive, integrity setting, ACL, organization policy, firewall/proxy setting, package registration, or sandbox service was modified by the diagnostic investigation of this episode. The Windows repair events attribute the activation caller to Explorer.
- Source/cached files and package placement warrant investigation, but a non-system-drive installation is a condition, not a proven cause. No C:-only A/B test or filesystem migration was performed.
- No preparation-phase 120-second timeout was identified for this specific ordinary-relaunch episode. Do not conflate it with the prior organization-settings deadline issue.
- No app Reset, cache/history deletion, sign-out, reinstallation, or destructive project/memory operation was attempted.

Related reports, not confirmed duplicates:

- Same-installation answer-selection keyboard-copy report: #52492; completed-answer visibility report: #52493. These document why the user had been relaunching; they are not established causes of the activation failure.

- #48729: first-launch local runtime preparation / organization-settings deadline. Existing comments also document newer preparation-phase failures; this report adds a different activation/registration episode.
- #38843: same-version registration repairs during an update loop, plus a permanently suspended process. This incident eventually opened without manually resuming a process, and neither an endless update loop nor permanently suspended process has been established here.

Please correlate clean tray exit, subsequent Explorer activation, same-version `RepairAppRegistrationOption` operations, sandbox-service reinstallation, and activation results. If related to an existing defect, please identify the supported fix and affected/fixed builds. Recovery on a warm launch is not sufficient evidence that subsequent updates or ordinary relaunches are fixed.

Submitted with the affected user's explicit authorization. No raw Windows/desktop logs, private conversation screenshots, chat/project contents, memory data, credentials, usernames, SIDs, or personal paths are attached.
